clue.text: Almost discarded footwear for robes

indicators.note: almost means the word is not quite complete, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: discarded means cast, as in cast off
socks are footwear

explanation.surface: Someone nearly threw out their footwear in exchange for some robes.
explanation.definitionFit: Cassocks are the long robes worn by clergy and choristers.

clue.text: A top University lecturer's opening N company in Mexican city

parts.note: a cap is a top, as on a bottle

indicators.note: a word's opening is its first letter

explanation.surface: A senior university lecturer joins a company in a Mexican city.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray 'N' as held is OCR noise for an ampersand joining the pieces; it gives no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Acapulco is a resort city on Mexico's Pacific coast.

clue.text: Move quickly to flatten an insect?

definitions.meaning: a colloquial order to hurry up, especially in a car
literally, to tread on a bug and squash it

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is slang for accelerating, and literally describes treading on something.

clue.text: It stops either end of crack?

definitions.text: It stops either end of crack?

indicators.note: to stop is to plug a gap, so one piece fills the gap in the other
the ends of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: either goes with or, so it gives OR

explanation.surface: Something plugs each end of a split.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stops' puts OR inside C and K, the first and last letters of 'crack'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cork is a stopper pushed into the neck of a bottle.

clue.text: Important people's records turned up

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: laic means of the lay people, as opposed to the clergy
EPs are extended-play records

explanation.surface: The records of VIPs have been found again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' turns LAIC + EPS into SPECIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Special is a synonym of important, as in a special occasion.

clue.text: One in quiz satisfied about way to answer

indicators.note: about means surrounding the other pieces

parts.note: content means satisfied
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A quiz player is pleased with how they got the answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the satisfied word around the way and the answer; 'to' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A contestant is someone taking part in a quiz or competition.

clue.text: Composer's triumph, going to Ireland

indicators.note: going to means added after the first piece

parts.note: a coup is a triumph
Erin is a poetic name for Ireland

explanation.surface: A composer has a great success on a trip to Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Francois Couperin was a French Baroque composer; the possessive 's is a link meaning has.

clue.text: Earnest figure in a vestment?

definitions.meaning: Canon ... is a character in Wilde's play The Importance of Being Earnest
a sleeveless outer garment worn by a priest at Mass

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a priestly garment and the canon in Wilde's comedy.

clue.text: Dismiss dog that's caught out repeatedly

indicators.note: repeatedly means the result is given twice
out means the letter is removed

parts.note: a pooch is a dog
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone sends away a dog that keeps getting caught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' drops C from POOCH to give POOH, and 'repeatedly' doubles it.
explanation.definitionFit: To pooh-pooh something is to dismiss it scornfully as unimportant.

clue.text: Unconstrained aim of the NHS?

definitions.meaning: the NHS, Britain's National Health Service, aims to give medical care at no charge

explanation.definitionFit: Carefree means untroubled, and read as two words it describes care given for nothing.

clue.text: Animal when going round mountain finds flowering trees

indicators.note: going round means surrounding the other piece

parts.note: a cat is an animal
as can mean when
an alp is a mountain

explanation.surface: An animal circling a mountain comes upon flowering trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Catalpas are trees with large leaves and showy white flowers.

clue.text: Doctors' families seen around in here in France

definitions.note: the possessive apostrophe is a link; the plural matches

indicators.note: seen around means the families surround the other pieces

parts.note: clans are families
taken as written
ici is French for here

explanation.surface: Doctors' families are spotted in this place, in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen around' has the families enclose the other pieces; 'Doctors'' looks possessive but its apostrophe is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Clinicians are doctors who treat patients directly.

clue.text: Descriptive of lines of pilgrims?

parts.note: not a queue of travellers but the verse of the Canterbury Tales, whose pilgrims tell the stories

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes the poetry of the author of the Canterbury Tales.

clue.text: Sour character beginning to remonstrate aboard taxi

indicators.note: aboard means inside the vehicle

parts.note: a cab is a taxi

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A grumpy person starts complaining in a taxi.
explanation.definitionFit: A crab is an informal word for a bad-tempered person.

clue.text: French writer: the fellow has pull, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the words are spoken and sound like the answer

parts.note: cock is slang for a fellow, and tow means pull

explanation.surface: A French writer has influence, so it is said.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean Cocteau was a French poet, novelist and film-maker.

clue.text: Bird-dog's drink?

parts.note: a cock is a male bird
to dog is to follow, or tail

explanation.surface: A drink for a gun dog.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a bird-dog, a gun dog; it splits into a bird and a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A cocktail is a mixed alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Variety of limecast it may cover minute, walls

indicators.note: a variety is a different arrangement, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Some kind of lime mortar may coat walls.
explanation.definitionFit: Clematis is a climbing plant often grown up walls and fences.

clue.text: Intonation of start of chant excellent; in middle, end, awful

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter
in middle means put inside the other piece

parts.note: ace means excellent

indicators.note: awful means the letters are a mess, rearranged

explanation.surface: A chant starts well and ends badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end' looks like a pointer to final letters, but it is the fodder 'awful' rearranges to DEN; 'in middle' sets that inside the excellent word.
explanation.definitionFit: Cadence is the rise and fall of the voice in speech.

clue.text: Badly-looked-after wife to regret taking up unknown risk

indicators.note: in a down entry, taking up means reading from bottom to top

parts.note: to rue is to regret
Y is a mathematical unknown
to dice, as in dice with death, is to risk

explanation.surface: A neglected wife regrets the gamble she took.
explanation.walkthrough: Orpheus lost her by looking back as he led her out of the underworld, hence 'Badly-looked-after'.
explanation.definitionFit: Eurydice was the wife of Orpheus in Greek myth.

clue.text: Mostly a pain in the neck about difficulty, becoming angry

indicators.note: about means surrounding the other piece
mostly means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a crick is a painful stiff neck
a hole is a difficulty, as in being in a hole

explanation.surface: An annoying person is causing trouble and getting cross.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' drops the last letter of the pain in the neck, and 'about' wraps it round the difficulty; 'becoming' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Choleric means hot-tempered, from choler, the humour of anger.

clue.text: Whales etc, at sea — excellent opening for angler

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: ace means excellent

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An angler gets a fine start at sea among whales and other creatures.
explanation.definitionFit: Cetacea is the order of marine mammals that includes whales.

clue.text: Men on board were triumphant

definitions.meaning: an old past tense of crow, to exult in victory

explanation.definitionFit: A crew mans a ship, and crew is an old past tense of crow, to gloat.

clue.text: City not backing Catholic author

parts.note: Chester is a city in Cheshire

indicators.note: backing means the word is reversed

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A city takes no part in supporting a Catholic writer.
explanation.definitionFit: G. K. Chesterton was an English writer who converted to Catholicism.

clue.text: Drink, type of vermouth, knocked back by a girl I've just met

indicators.note: knocked back means the word is reversed, as a drink is knocked back

parts.note: It is short for Italian vermouth, as in gin and it
from the West Side Story song, I've just met a girl named Maria

explanation.surface: A drink of vermouth is downed by someone with a new girlfriend.
explanation.definitionFit: Tia Maria is a coffee liqueur.

clue.text: Lump fish seen round lake

indicators.note: seen round means the fish surrounds the other piece

parts.note: a cod is a fish

explanation.surface: A lumpfish is spotted around a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A clod is a lump of earth or clay.

clue.text: Dog beside tracks? It's mine

indicators.note: beside means placed next to the first piece

parts.note: a collie is a dog
RY is the abbreviation for railway, laid on tracks

explanation.surface: A dog by the railway line belongs to the speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A colliery is a coal mine; 'mine' looks like the possessive.

clue.text: One fool I took in, having special knowledge

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a nit is a fool
ate means took in, as food

explanation.surface: I fooled someone and I took them in.
explanation.definitionFit: An initiate, as an adjective, is someone admitted to secret knowledge.

clue.text: They observe an interview

definitions.meaning: a formal meeting with an important person, such as the Pope

explanation.definitionFit: An audience is both the spectators and a formal hearing granted by a dignitary.
